full_judgment:
Md. Awlad Ali, J: This Rule arises but of an arear 21.7.2000 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat rejecting the miscellaneous case under Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. Shortly, stated, facts are that the respondent No. 2 Pubali Bank Ltd. obtained an exparte decree for a sum of Tk. 3,22,797/- on 16.9.99 against the respondent No. 3 M. A. Jalil. The bank put the decree in execution being Title Execution Case No. 60/2000 for realisation of decretal dues by selling the mortgaged property. The property to be sold was attached by the order of the court in execution proceeding. There after the present petitioner filed Misc. Case No. 22/2001 in the Court of Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka under Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for releasing the property from the order of attachment stating inter alia, that the respondent No. 3 M. A. Jaill took loan from the respondent bank creating mortgage of the property of the petitioner showing that the said M. A. Jalil obtained a deed from the petitioner nos. 2-4 purporting to have purchased the property. Further stated that the respondent No. 3 had never been in possession of the property to be sold. 

 3.The respondent bank has filed affidavit-in-opposition stating that the judgment-debtor M. A. Jalil mortgaged the property to the bank and the deed stands in the name of M.A. Jalil. The learned Arth Rin Adalat after hearing the parties and receiving the evidence by impugned order dated 21.7.2000 dismissed the miscellaneous case with a finding that the mortgage deed stood in the name of M.A. Jalil and that the petitioner have not been able to establish their claim of title and possession although the petitioner no. 1 being the divorced wife has been in possession of the property comprising the purchase deed in the name of M. A. Jalil.
